newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon to hold parliamentary poll in November.
newsitem.headline: Gabon to hold parliamentary poll in November.

text.p: Gabon has set November 17 as the date for the first round of its much-delayed parliamentary election, after President Omar Bongo said the delay threatened to slow economic recovery in the Central African nation.

A government decree made public on Monday (eds correct) set the date of the second round as December 1 but opposition members of the National Electoral Commission say that November is too soon and leaves too little time to organise properly.

The elections are designed to build on a 1994 deal struck in Paris between the government and the opposition after bloody social and political unrest that followed Bongo's disputed election to a five-year term as president in 1993.
Bongo said on state television on Sunday that the outside world was wondering why the elections had been delayed.

"Because of the delay in the electoral process, our country risks falling behind economically," he said. "We must do everything possible to complete the electoral process. That will enable us to focus on the economic tasks awaiting us."

Last week the opposition vice-chairman of the commission, Mengome Atome, said that with municipal elections on October 20, a November date left too little time to prepare for parliamentary polls. He said commission chairman Nguema Essono, named by Bongo, had unilaterally declared the date.
Under the Paris accords, the parliamentary poll should have been help early in 1996. Parliament's mandate expired in May.

Five people died in opposition unrest triggered by Bongo's election victory in 1993. Further clashes followed in 1994, in part to back pay demands following the devaluation of the CFA franc used in Gabon and much of French-speaking Africa. The official death toll was nine, the opposition put it at 38.
